mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep inching upward from their current depressed levels, weekday trip chaining will increase and lift retail visits within four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting recovery stalls or if retail remains detached from transit and workplace recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is around -46 to -47 and TRANSIT improved from -49.7 to -45.6 over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean after a continued rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, or it falls despite both proxies improving together.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in PARKS mobility signals warmer outdoor conditions and more discretionary out-of-home activity, which spills into nearby retail visits with a one- to two-week lag. The effect fails if park visits rise for reasons unrelated to consumer foot traffic, such as isolated park use without broader outing intensity.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week from a negative baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -30.1 at t-1w to -18.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: A week-on-week PARKS jump of 8 points or more is not followed by a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next 14 days than over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL time with flat WORKPLACES implies more time spent at home and fewer discretionary shopping trips, which pushes retail mobility lower over the next month. The hypothesis fails if residential time rises but retail also rises, indicating home-based time is not substituting away from shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 13.0 to 11.1 while WORKPLACES stayed near -46 to -47
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to its last-4-week mean even when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES stays flat or weak.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES marks a loosening access regime that expands weekday retail opportunities, but only after the pair crosses a recovery threshold. The effect fails if either series rebounds alone without the other, because the retail response requires joint access and activity recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by at least 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -48.0 to -45.6 while WORKPLACES was roughly unchanged near -46.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by at least 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is already recovering and GROCERY_PHARM also softens less, weekend errand bundles become more common and support retail activity in the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if park recovery is isolated and does not coincide with a broadening of local errand mobility.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior two-week average while GROCERY_PHARM is no worse than 5 points below its prior two-week average
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -22.4 to -18.6 while PARKS jumped from -30.1 to -18.9
failure_condition: After park recovery with stable grocery-pharmacy mobility, RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in TRANSIT relative to WORKPLACES suppresses spontaneous shopping because fewer workers convert commute trips into retail stops. This predicts retail will stay below its recent mean for four weeks unless transit recovers materially. The hypothesis fails if retail rebounds while transit remains deeply negative.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -50 to -45.6 while WORKPLACES stayed near -46 to -47
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its last-4-week mean during a two-week spell with TRANSIT below -40.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in GROCERY_PHARM combined with unchanged or weaker WORKPLACES indicates more local, non-commute trip activity that substitutes for retail visits rather than amplifying them. Over one week, this should pressure RETAIL_REC down if the grocery increase is not matched by transit recovery.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while TRANSIT does not improve
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved steadily from -22.4 to -18.6 while TRANSIT remained very negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even though GROCERY_PHARM increases and TRANSIT does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tighter-informal-restriction regime, even modest gains in parks and residential time will redirect activity away from shopping districts, so retail remains weaker over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if retail improves despite park recovery and elevated home time, showing restrictions are no longer shaping trip allocation.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive near 11 to 13 while PARKS rebounded sharply at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite sustained positive RESIDENTIAL and recovering PARKS.
